Read a streamed response body, its trailers, or stop reading

Source: R/response.R
zu_resp_read.Rd

A response from zu_perform() with stream = TRUE arrives with its body unread (§65.4). zu_resp_read() returns the next piece of it: up to n decoded bytes, waiting for at least one, and a raw vector of length 0 at the end. Over HTTP/2 the server is allowed to send only as far ahead as the caller reads, so a body nobody reads holds the server at one flow-control window. max_body is enforced across the whole body, and every wait is bounded by the request's timeout afresh and interruptible with Ctrl-C.

Usage

zu_resp_read(resp, n = 65536)

zu_resp_abort(resp)

zu_resp_trailers(resp, name = NULL)

Arguments

resp

A zu_response.

n

Maximum bytes to return.

name

A field name, or NULL for all of them.

Value

zu_resp_read() a raw vector; zu_resp_abort() resp, invisibly; zu_resp_trailers() a named character vector (name = NULL) or a character vector, length 0 when the field is absent, or NULL while a streamed body is unread.

Details

zu_resp_abort() stops reading (§65.5). Over HTTP/2 it resets the stream (RST_STREAM(CANCEL)) and keeps the connection for the next request; over HTTP/1.1 it closes the connection. A second call, or a call on a body read to its end, does nothing. A later zu_resp_read() raises zu_cancelled_error.

zu_resp_trailers() returns the header fields sent after the body: HTTP/2 trailers, or a chunked HTTP/1.1 body's trailer section (§65.3, D-91). gRPC carries its status there. Matching is case-insensitive as in zu_resp_header(). For a streamed response they are known once zu_resp_read() has returned the end of the body; before that, and after zu_resp_abort() or a failed read, zu_resp_trailers() returns NULL: the trailers are unknown, which is not the same as none (D-98).

A response that was not streamed by its transport (a mock, a cassette) reads from its stored body, in pieces of n, and follows the same rules, trailers included: build one with zu_response(trailers = ). So code written against zu_resp_read() runs against zu_mock_transport() and cassettes unchanged. A streamed response has no body to hand to zu_resp_raw(), zu_resp_text() or zu_resp_json(), which refuse it.

Examples

fake <- zu_mock_transport(function(req) zu_response(200L, body = "hello"))
r <- zu_perform(
  zu_request("GET", "https://example.com/"),
  client = zu_client(transport = fake),
  stream = TRUE
)
zu_resp_read(r, 3)
#> [1] 68 65 6c
zu_resp_read(r, 3)
#> [1] 6c 6f
zu_resp_read(r, 3)
#> raw(0)
